skill.displayName: 波龙股神量化交易系统

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: bowlong-quant-aio
Version: 2.0.0

The bundle is a comprehensive quantitative trading framework for the Chinese A-share and futures markets, providing modules for stock selection, backtesting, and trade execution. It interfaces with local trading terminals (Huaxin QMT and Wenhua WH8) via standard HTTP APIs and utilizes legitimate financial data sources like Tushare and Akshare. While the scripts handle sensitive credentials (trading passwords and API tokens) and include a Telegram notification feature for risk alerts, these capabilities are transparently documented and strictly aligned with the stated purpose of financial automation. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection was identified.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate quantitative trading toolkit, but the declared requirements in the registry do not fully match the runtime instructions and files (undeclared credentials are referenced), so you should review before installing or providing secrets.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (A股/期货 quant system) align with included scripts (stock_picker, backtest, risk_monitor, executors for Huaxin/文华). Required binary (python3) and use of market-data token (TUSHARE_TOKEN) are coherent for this purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to run local Python scripts and edit config files. The runtime instructions and examples stay within trading workflows (select/backtest/execute/monitor) and reference local trading APIs or local HTTP endpoints for broker gateways; nothing in SKILL.md instructs the agent to read unrelated system files or phone home to unexpected endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only plus bundled Python scripts. No remote downloads or archive extraction are specified; risk from install mechanism is low. Dependencies are typical Python packages.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry requires only TUSHARE_TOKEN, but SKILL.md, README and config files reference many additional environment variables and secrets (QMT_ACCOUNT, QMT_PASSWORD, WH8_ACCOUNT, WH8_PASSWORD, TB_ACCOUNT/TB_PASSWORD, PUSH_TOKEN/PUSH_CHAT_ID, etc.). Those are legitimate for real trading connectors, but the mismatch between declared required env vars and actual usage is an inconsistency and raises risk if users assume only TUSHARE_TOKEN will be needed. Several env vars are sensitive (passwords/tokens) — ensure you only provide them to trusted code and use test accounts first.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not force-included (always:false) and does not request platform-wide persistence. It can perform autonomous actions by default (disable-model-invocation:false) but that's normal for skills; nothing requests modification of other skills or global agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is a full trading toolkit and the code appears to implement the advertised features. However: (1) registry metadata lists only TUSHARE_TOKEN while the code/configs reference many other credentials (broker accounts, passwords, push tokens). Treat that as an inconsistency — the skill can use your trading/account credentials if you add them. (2) Only provide real exchange/broker credentials after you audit the code and test thoroughly in paper/simulated mode. The executors default to local HTTP endpoints (127.0.0.1) for broker APIs — prefer running those broker gateways locally and ensure they are not exposed to the public internet. (3) Run the code in an isolated environment or VM and start with simulated accounts; inspect scripts/executor_*.py for any unexpected network destinations or hard-coded remote hosts before using live funds. (4) If you plan to enable Telegram or other push channels, create dedicated bot/chat credentials. (5) If you need higher assurance, ask the author for a signed release or corroborating GitHub repo history before supplying any secrets.
